question: Will the Republicans win the Maine Senate race in 2026?
description:
This market will resolve according to the winner of the 2026 midterm Maine U.S. Senate election, inclusive of any run-offs.

A candidate shall be considered to represent a party in the event that he or she is the nominee of the party in question. Candidates other than the Democratic or Republican nominee (e.g., Greens, Libertarian, independent) may be added at a later date.

Candidates who run as independents will not be encompassed by the “Democrat” or “Republican” options regardless of any affiliation they may have with the party.

The resolution source for this market is the Associated Press, Fox News, and NBC. This market will resolve once all three sources call the race for the same candidate. If all three sources haven’t called the race in this state for the same candidate, this market will resolve based on the official certification.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent polling averages show Democrat Troy Jackson holding a narrow lead over incumbent Republican Susan Collins in the November 2026 Maine Senate race, reflecting shifts after the Democratic nomination process. Jackson secured the nomination in late July following Graham Platner’s withdrawal amid allegations, consolidating support from progressives including endorsements from Sen. Bernie Sanders. Multiple July and August surveys, including those from the University of New Hampshire and Senate Majority PAC, place Jackson ahead by 2–4 points among likely voters, driven by strength with women and independents in a state where such blocs often decide outcomes. Collins, a moderate with a history of outperforming early deficits, maintains a path through turnout and cross-party appeal, though traders appear to weigh the current polling edge and nomination stability more heavily in assigning Jackson the higher implied probability. The contest remains fluid with roughly 10 weeks until Election Day.
